explanations.explanation: That's what He says, friend. “I revealed Myself to those who did not ask for Me; I was found by those who did not seek Me.” (Isaiah 65:1) They weren't asking and they weren't seeking, and He still revealed Himself. He says, “Here I am! Here I am!” to a nation that did not call His name.

No, friend, it goes the other way. The LORD says He revealed Himself to those who did not ask for Him. He also says, “All day long I have held out My hands…” (Isaiah 65:2). Nobody gets a door slammed in this verse.

explanations.answer: He waits for them to ask first
explanations.explanation: You'd expect that, wouldn't you? But the LORD says He was found by those who did not seek Him. He didn't wait for the first move. “To a nation that did not call My name, I said, ‘Here I am! Here I am!’” (Isaiah 65:1).

That's it. The LORD says they walk in the wrong path and “…follow their own imaginations…” (Isaiah 65:2). Picture me baking from a recipe I made up at two in the morning. I'd feel REAL sure of myself right up until the oven opened.
Not here, friend. The verse never mentions kings giving orders. It says they follow “…their own imaginations…” (Isaiah 65:2). The path they're on comes from inside them.
Egypt isn't in this verse. The LORD says these people follow their own imaginations. All day long He's holding out His hands to them while they walk that path (Isaiah 65:2).
Yep, friend. The LORD says they are “…sacrificing in the gardens and burning incense on altars of brick…” (Isaiah 65:3). Gardens and brick altars are the places He names. That's the answer here.
That's not what the LORD describes. He says they sacrifice “…in the gardens…” and burn incense “…on altars of brick…” (Isaiah 65:3). The temple altar doesn't come up in this verse.
The river isn't mentioned here. The LORD says they sacrifice in the gardens. He also says they burn incense on altars of brick (Isaiah 65:3).

That's the line, friend. “Such people are smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.” (Isaiah 65:5) They say, “Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!” The LORD says that's what such people are to Him.
The LORD says the opposite. People who say “Keep to yourself; do not come near me, for I am holier than you!” are “…smoke in My nostrils…” (Isaiah 65:5). That's not a sweet smell by any stretch.
No crown here, friend. For these people the LORD says, “…smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.” (Isaiah 65:5) Their holier-than-you talk doesn't earn them one.

True, friend. The LORD says they are “…smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.” (Isaiah 65:5) You get both in one line, the smoke and the fire. The fire is the part that burns all day long.

It's actually true, friend. The full line is “…smoke in My nostrils, a fire that burns all day long.” (Isaiah 65:5) The fire is right there beside the smoke. Easy to miss when the smoke gets all the attention.
The LORD says the opposite, friend. “I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will pay it back into their laps…” (Isaiah 65:6) He doesn't stay quiet here. He speaks and says what He will do.

False is right. The LORD says, “I will not keep silent, but I will repay; I will pay it back into their laps…” (Isaiah 65:6) His people had asked whether He would keep silent (Isaiah 64:12). Here He speaks.

That's what He says about them, friend. “Because they burned incense on the mountains and scorned Me on the hills, I will measure into their laps full payment for their former deeds.” (Isaiah 65:7) The mountains and hills are where He says it happened. He also says this repayment is for their iniquities and for those of their fathers.

explanations.answer: Hid their silver from the priests
explanations.explanation: Silver and priests don't come up in this verse. The LORD says they burned incense on the mountains and scorned Him on the hills (Isaiah 65:7). That's what the repayment is for.
No armies in this verse, friend. The LORD says, “Because they burned incense on the mountains and scorned Me on the hills…” (Isaiah 65:7). That's the charge He names.

That's the picture, friend. Men say, “Do not destroy it, for it contains a blessing…” (Isaiah 65:8). Then the LORD says, “so I will act on behalf of My servants; I will not destroy them all.” (Isaiah 65:8)
The king isn't in this picture. The men say to leave it alone “…for it contains a blessing…” (Isaiah 65:8). That's why the cluster gets saved.
The verse doesn't say anything about ripeness. It says new wine is found in the cluster and the men say, “Do not destroy it, for it contains a blessing…” (Isaiah 65:8) The blessing is the reason.

True. The LORD says, “My elect will possess My mountains, and My servants will dwell there.” (Isaiah 65:9) He also promises descendants from Jacob and heirs from Judah in the same verse. They get a place to live, friend.
It's actually true. The LORD says, “My elect will possess My mountains, and My servants will dwell there.” (Isaiah 65:9) Dwelling is exactly what He promises His servants.

Yep. Sharon becomes a pasture for flocks and the Valley of Achor a resting place for herds, “…for My people who seek Me.” (Isaiah 65:10) Seeking is the word here. Verse 1 spoke of people who did not seek Him and were found anyway, and verse 10 speaks of His people who seek Him.
Forgetting belongs to the other group. The LORD says the land is “…for My people who seek Me.” (Isaiah 65:10) The ones who “…forget My holy mountain…” come up next, in verse 11.

Scorning is something the LORD said earlier about those who “…scorned Me on the hills…” (Isaiah 65:7) The pasture and the resting place are “…for My people who seek Me.” (Isaiah 65:10) That's the word here.

That's the one. The LORD says they “…set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny…” (Isaiah 65:11) Fortune gets a table while His holy mountain gets forgotten. I'd lay out a nice spread for a plate of cookies before I'd do that for luck.
Baal, a false god, isn't named in these verses. The LORD says they “…set a table for Fortune…” (Isaiah 65:11) That's the name on the table.
Molech, a false god, doesn't show up in this verse. The LORD says they “…set a table for Fortune and fill bowls of mixed wine for Destiny…” (Isaiah 65:11) Those are the two named here.

explanations.answer: He called and they did not answer
explanations.explanation: That's what He says. “…I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen; you did evil in My sight and chose that in which I did not delight.” (Isaiah 65:12) He called and spoke, and they didn't answer or listen. Friend, that's a lot of knocking on a door.

explanations.answer: They forgot to bring an offering
explanations.explanation: The LORD doesn't say that. He says, “…I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen…” (Isaiah 65:12) He also says they chose what He did not delight in.
Treaties aren't mentioned here. The LORD says, “…I called and you did not answer, I spoke and you did not listen…” (Isaiah 65:12). That's the reason He gives.

The LORD says it the other way around. “My servants will eat, but you will go hungry; My servants will drink, but you will go thirsty…” (Isaiah 65:13) His servants are the ones who eat. The ones who forsook Him go hungry.
False is right. The Lord GOD says, “My servants will eat, but you will go hungry…” (Isaiah 65:13) The servants eat and the others go hungry. He puts the two side by side on purpose.

explanations.answer: They will be put to shame
explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. “My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 65:13) One side rejoices and the other side is put to shame. The same verse says His servants will eat while the others go hungry, and drink while the others go thirsty. No middle ground in that verse.
The Lord GOD says it's a contrast. “My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 65:13) That little word “but” is doing a lot of work. The others don't join the party.
That's not what the verse says. The Lord GOD says, “My servants will rejoice, but you will be put to shame.” (Isaiah 65:13) Shame is what He names for them.

True. The Lord GOD says, “but to His servants He will give another name.” (Isaiah 65:15) The others leave their name behind as a curse for His chosen ones, and His servants get a new one. Me, I got a name carved in my handle, and that was plenty.
It's actually true, friend. The Lord GOD says, “but to His servants He will give another name.” (Isaiah 65:15) The new name goes to His servants. The old name is what the other group leaves behind.

That's the word, friend. “For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from My sight.” (Isaiah 65:16) Forgotten is exactly what the LORD says about them. The verse also says the troubles are hidden from His sight.
The verse says the opposite. “For the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from My sight.” (Isaiah 65:16) Forgotten is the word the LORD uses. The troubles don't hang around.

Written shows up earlier, when the LORD says, “…it is written before Me…” (Isaiah 65:6) Here the word is different. The verse says, “…the former troubles will be forgotten and hidden from My sight.” (Isaiah 65:16) Forgotten is the word that fits the blank.
